prompt: A rancher has $120$ meters of fence to build a rectangular pen against a long barn. The barn forms one side, so only three sides need fence. What is the maximum possible area of the pen, in square meters?
hint: Let $x$ be the length of each side perpendicular to the barn. Two of those plus one parallel side use all $120$ m.

hints.text: Let $x$ be the length of each side perpendicular to the barn. Two of those plus one parallel side use all $120$ m.
The parallel side is $120 - 2x$, so the area is $A(x) = x(120 - 2x) = 120x - 2x^2$. Set the derivative $A'(x)$ equal to $0$ and solve for $x$.
Solving $120 - 4x = 0$ gives $x = 30$. The pen is $30$ by $60$, so the maximum area is $1800$ square meters.

explanation: The fence gives the constraint $2x + y = 120$, so the side along the barn is $y = 120 - 2x$.
The area is $A(x) = x(120 - 2x) = 120x - 2x^2$. Then $A'(x) = 120 - 4x = 0$ at $x = 30$, and $A'' = -4 < 0$ confirms a maximum.
Then $y = 120 - 60 = 60$, and the maximum area is $30 \cdot 60 = 1800$ square meters. The free barn side lets the pen be twice as long as it is deep.

alternativeExplanations.title: Split the fence in half
steps: In barn problems the best pen uses half the fence across and half along. Here the two sides touching the barn share $60$ m and the side parallel to it uses $60$ m.
Check with neighbors: depth $25$ gives $25 \cdot 70 = 1750$ and depth $35$ gives $35 \cdot 50 = 1750$, both less than depth $30$ gives.
So each perpendicular side is $30$ m, the parallel side is $60$ m, and the largest area is $30 \cdot 60 = 1800$ square meters.
